rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that during Abu Talib’s illness, Quraysh complained about Muhammad’s attacks on their gods; he offered one word for Arab submission and Persian tribute, named the testimony of God’s oneness, and they recoiled, prompting this passage’s revelation.
rows.anchor: Ebû Tâlib hastalandığı zaman Kureyşten bir heyet geldi, içlerinde Ebû Cehil de vardı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No transmitted report counts Ṣād as a verse; Elmalılı notes it is written as one letter and may be read as the letter’s name, a past verb from ṣ-y-d, or an imperative from ṣ-d-a.
rows.anchor: Sâd, bunu âyet sayan rivayet yoktur. Yazılışı itibariyle bir harf, okunuşu itibariyle bir isim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Ṣād is a disconnected letter, it is presented, like the other such letters, as a challenge and a sign of the Qur’an’s inimitability.
rows.anchor: Harf olduğuna göre diğer mukatta‘âtta geçtiği üzere tehaddî ve i‘câz yoluyla serdedilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority take Ṣād as the name of this sura; Elmalılı also allows that it may be only a symbol.
rows.anchor: Ekserin kavlince bu sûrenin ismidir. Mücerred bir remz olması da melhuzdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a symbol, Ṣād may first evoke sirat, found in the Fatiha, and words from the ṣ-d-q root, such as God’s truthfulness or Muhammad as truthful.
rows.anchor: Fâtiha’da bu harf ile alâkadar “sırat” kelimesi vardır. “Sıdk” maddesi de bu remzin ilk ihtar edeceği kelimelerdendir.

rows.speaker: Hasen
rows.claim: Hasan derives Ṣād as an imperative from musādat, the reciprocal form of ṣādā, meaning to answer or echo.
rows.anchor: Hasen’den rivayet olunduğuna göre “sâdâ”nın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because ṣadā is an echo or response, the imperative can mean to echo the Qur’an and put its content into practice.
rows.anchor: “Sadâ” karşılık vermektir. Onun için sesin aksettiği yerden verilen karşılığa “sadâ” denir.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Ṣād as the sea over which the Throne of the Merciful rested before night and day existed; Elmalılı cites Hud 11:7.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan bir rivayete göre “Sâd” gece ve gündüz yokken Arş-ı Rahmân’ın üzerinde bulunduğu deryânın ismidir.

rows.speaker: Said b. Cübeyr
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr identifies Ṣād as the sea where God revives the dead between the two trumpet blasts.
rows.anchor: Said b. Cübeyr’den; Allah teâlâ’nın iki nefha arasında mevtâyı ihyâ buyurduğu deryânın ismidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the two sea reports unusual but subtle, Elmalılı suggests Ṣād may carry an oath sense, with wa-al-Qur’an then serving as a coordinated phrase.
rows.anchor: Bu iki rivayet garîb olmakla beraber latîftir. Bunlarda “Sâd” kasem mânasını da tazammun edebilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr in the description of the Qur’an can mean renown and honor, admonition and warning (including law, promises, threats, and instructive stories), or teaching what religion requires.
rows.anchor: “Zikr” nâmı anılmak, şeref ü şan mânasına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath’s answer is omitted: Muhammad is truthful in his mission, what he is told is true, and the Qur’an’s promises and warnings will come to pass; bal is attached to that omitted answer.
rows.anchor: Bu kasemin cevabı mahzuftur. بَلِ o mahzufa ma‘tuftur. Yani sen risaletinde sâdıksın, sana söylenen haktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers are trapped in pride and factional conflict: arrogance keeps them from accepting truth, while competing aims make them contend over various gods.
rows.anchor: bir izzet ile şikāk içinde kendilerini bir onur, kibir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cried out in repentance when they saw destruction, but it was already too late to escape.
rows.anchor: Çığırıştılar yani helâki gördükleri vakit tevbe edip “aman yâ Rabbi” diye bağırıştılar, feryad ettiler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı explains lāt as lā and takes the phrase to mean that the time for escape had passed.
rows.anchor: Fakat o vakit, yahut o çığrışma kurtulacak zaman değildi, kaçamak ihtimâli kalmamıştı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In his rendering, an admonisher from among them is a prophet who awakens them, and the unbelievers call him a sorcerer and liar.
rows.anchor: İçlerinden kendilerine uyandırıcı bir peygamber geldiğine şaştılar da dediler ki kâfirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask whether Muhammad has denied divinity to all but one God. The polytheistic mind cannot imagine one deity meeting varied human needs and misses that all sovereignty belongs to Him, so it marvels at monotheism.
rows.anchor: İlâhları hep bir ilâh mı kıldı yani لاَ اِلٰهَ اِ َّلا اللّٰهُ diye hepsinden ulûhiyeti nefyetti de yalnız birine mi kasr etti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the elite as rushing off and urging one another to remain steadfast with their gods, calling the matter something desired or intended.
rows.anchor: İçlerinden o heyet de fırladı şöyle: “İlâhlarınız üzerinde sabr u sebat edin,

words: مَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِى ٱلْمِلَّةِ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He renders millat al-ākhira as the other or later religious community and identifies it here with Christianity, the latest community before Islam, which accepted the Trinity.
rows.anchor: Biz bunu millet-i âhirede işitmedik “millet-i âhire” diğer millet, yahut sonraki millet demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikri means My Qur’an; azābi means My punishment, with the possessive yā omitted after the kasra, as in ʿiqābi.
rows.anchor: “azâbî” demektir, kesre ile “yâ”dan iktifâ olunmuştur

words: مِّنَ ٱلْأَحْزَابِ جُندٌۭ مَّا هُنَالِكَ مَهْزُومٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh are a ragged remnant of past coalitions against prophets, spiritually disunited and doomed to defeat. The verse also signals Quraysh’s defeats beginning at Badr and the need for a well ordered army to emerge from a well ordered people.
rows.anchor: Onlar burada ahzâbdan kalma bozuk bir ordu döküntüsü yani eskiden peygamberlere karşı toplanmış, mahvolmuş muhtelif hiziblerden bakıyye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders God’s opening a person’s breast to Islam as being on light from the Lord, and describes hearts hardened from God’s remembrance as hard.
rows.anchor: Demek ki her kimin Allah bağrını İslâm’a açmış ise işte o Rabbinden bir nûr üzerinde değil mi? O hâlde vay o Allah’ın zikrinden kalbleri katılara!

words: تَقْشَعِرُّ مِنْهُ جُلُودُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He renders the Qur’an’s description as an ‘ikizli, âhenkli’ book and says the God-fearing first shiver, then their skins and hearts soften to God’s remembrance.
rows.anchor: ikizli, âhenkli bir kitap. Ondan Rablerine saygısı olanların derileri ürperir, sonra derileri de kalbleri de Allah’ın zikrine yumuşar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He pictures the wrongdoer as using his face to shield himself from the evil punishment on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: o kötü azâbı yüzü ile koruyacak kimse ne olur?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the verse as asking whether God is not sufficient for His servant, while they frighten the Prophet with those besides Him; whoever God leads astray has no guide.
rows.anchor: Allah kuluna kâfî değil mi? Durmuşlar da seni ondan beridekilerle korkutuyorlar, her kimi ki Allah şaşırtır artık ona hidâyet edecek yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He renders the pattern as a person praying to God in distress, then claiming a blessing was given because of his knowledge; the blessing is a test.
rows.anchor: Fakat insana bir sıkıntı dokunuverince Bize yalvarır, sonra kendisine tarafımızdan bir nimet bahşediverdiğimiz zaman da “o bana bir bilgi üzerine verildi” der.

words: فَمَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He renders the claim as one made by earlier people too, whose earnings did not save them.
rows.anchor: Onu bunlardan evvelkiler de söyledi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse looks back to the statement that the Prophet is not their guardian: God is, since He alone takes souls; Elmalılı says this is made explicit later in the sura.
rows.anchor: Bir kere kasr ile nihâyetteki وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيْهِم بِوَكِيلٍ kavline nâzırdır. Yani vekil sen değilsin Allah’tır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death and sleep provide an analogy for guidance and misguidance.
rows.anchor: ikincisi hidâyet ve dalâletin, hayat ve memat ile bir temsîlini iş‘âr eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse clarifies the earlier statement that the Prophet and his opponents will die and dispute before their Lord, confirming the reminder in Yunus 10:108 that guidance or error ultimately affects each person himself.
rows.anchor: tâ yukarıdaki إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌۭ وَإِنَّهُم مَّيِّتُونَ ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ عِندَ رَبِّكُمْ تَخْتَصِمُونَ kavlini bir nevi tavzih ile

rows.speaker: Sâhib-i Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf takes ‘selves’ as the whole soul-and-body entity; taking them means causing death by removing the conditions that sustain a living, sensing, perceiving being, since intellect alone is not described as dying or sleeping.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-i Keşşâf burada “enfüs”ten murad rûh ile beden mecmû‘u olduğuna kāil olarak demiştir ki

rows.speaker: diğer müfessirîn
rows.claim: Other exegetes, citing Ibn Abbas, take ‘selves’ as rational souls and explain taking them as severing their attachment and control over the body, inwardly and outwardly in death but outwardly only in sleep.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas Hazretleri’nden vârid olan bir rivayet vechile

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes the reasoning, discerning nafs from the breathing, moving ruh, comparing them to the sun and its rays; both are taken at death, but only the nafs during sleep.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas Hazretleri demiştir ki: “Âdem oğlunda bir nefis bir rûh vardır, aralarındaki fark Güneş ile şu‘âı gibidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the sun-and-ray comparison does not imply that the nafs and ruh are different substances.
rows.anchor: Güneş ile şu‘âını temsil getirmesi gösterir ki aralarında bir cevher farkı anlatmak istememiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He understands the nafs as the self-aware person, conscious of itself and what is within it, with the paired aspects of perceiver and perceived.
rows.anchor: Bizim anladığımız şudur: Nefis kendini duyan, kendine ve kendindekine vicdânı olan, yani ene şuuruna sâhip olan zattır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawaffi means taking something fully and completely; hence the soul’s complete retrieval by God is called tawaffi and death wafat, like fully honoring a trust by delivering it.
rows.anchor: Teveffî, bir şeyi vâfî olarak, yani kâmilen ve tamamıyla almak, selb etmektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Souls are not necessary beings: their consciousness is from God rather than inherent in their essence, and God can take them from themselves; Elmalılı compares this to 8:24.
rows.anchor: Nefisler vâcibü’l-vücud değildirler, onun için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God takes rational selves without destroying them, removing awareness and discernment: at death bodily attachment ceases and the soul is retained; in sleep, souls not destined to die are released until their appointed term.
rows.anchor: İşte nefsin teveffîsi, ölüm ve uyku hâllerinde olduğu gibi kendinden geçirilip akl u temyîzinin kendinden alınmasıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı raises how this verse’s attribution of taking souls to God relates to the earlier statements that the Angel of Death and God’s envoys take them; the excerpt ends before his answer.
rows.anchor: ٱلْمَوْتُ تَوَفَّتْهُ رُسُلُنَا وَهُمْ لَا يُفَرِّطُونَ
